target_customer: Cancer patients with solid tumours poorly served by immunotherapy; commercially, pharma partners and biotech investors who would license or acquire drug candidates
problem: Antibody drug candidates with several modifications at once (bispecific, multivalent, drug-conjugated) are slow and hard to discover, so novel mechanisms of action against known cancer targets are under-explored.
business_model: Therapeutics R&D company: discovery platform plus internal pipeline, partnering and licensing of drug candidates
product_category: Biotech, bispecific antibody drug conjugate (BsADC) discovery

founders.name: Arne Scheu
education: University of Oxford, DPhil in Biochemistry
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no prior employers.

founders.name: Irsyad Khairil
education: University of Oxford, DPhil in Biochemistry
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a pharma analyst with a protein engineering background; the company site names him CTO and co-founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Combining bispecificity, multivalency and drug conjugation in one discovery process needs synthetic protein biology, high-throughput screening and wet-lab capacity; candidates are still preclinical years after the 2021 batch.

defensibility.rationale: Platform know-how from Oxford research and a growing pipeline give some protection, but bispecific ADCs drew many well-funded entrants and a moat only forms once candidates reach the clinic.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found through the December 2025 alliance with Nona Biosciences; large players pursue ADCs, but no source shows them targeting this wedge directly.

market_need_then: Solid tumours poorly addressed by immunotherapy, and strong industry interest in antibody drug conjugates; the company's own site cites the need for drugs that attack tumours while sparing healthy tissue.

branding.name_origin: Company-quoted fragment suggests Valink is built from valency and linking, signalling a move beyond bispecificity alone; not fully confirmed because the quote is truncated in the sources.
branding.domain_note: Uses valinktx.com, a suffixed domain; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Patient-centred tagline 'Tougher on cancer, not on patients'

branding.brand_signature: Tagline 'Tougher on cancer, not on patients'; LiliumX kept as the platform name

rebrands.why: To mark the shift from a platform-building company to a therapeutics company, announced with a $7.8M raise

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B biotech brand known to investors and partners; sources show press releases but no community or consumer pull.

pivots.to: Therapeutics company with an internal pipeline (Valink)
pivots.why: Stated in the rebrand announcement as the transition from platform to therapeutics

outcome_analysis: Valink is an active Oxford spinout that spent about four years building its LiliumX platform, raised $7.8M in 2023 and $11.8M in 2025, and signed a discovery alliance with Nona Biosciences in December 2025. It is still preclinical, so the outcome is unresolved; the funding pace is modest for biotech, and its fate depends on pipeline data rather than on the YC batch.
notes: Stage of both rounds set to other: the company calls the 2025 round Pre-A, databases variously say seed or Series A. Investors of the 2023 round were not read in a source I opened. Aggregators give total raised of about 19.7 to 19.9M and conflicting headquarters. No competitor with a source dated near the early 2021 batch was found, so the list is empty; later bispecific ADC entrants such as Sidewinder and NEOK Bio emerged years later.
